content.value_statement: WordPress abilities can fail because of registration order, metadata, permissions, or REST configuration. This skill provides focused implementation and troubleshooting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides registration of ability categories and abilities in PHP.
Explains the required WordPress initialization hooks and their order.
Documents metadata for REST visibility and informational abilities.
Helps diagnose missing abilities, REST routes, dependencies, and caching issues.
Guides JavaScript clients that consume the WordPress abilities package.
limitations: Targets WordPress 6.9 or projects using a compatible Abilities API package.
Requires project context to choose plugin, theme, or must-use plugin placement.
Does not replace testing in a working WordPress environment.
Cannot determine permission rules without the application requirements.

use_cases.title: Register a plugin ability
use_cases.description: Create a namespaced category and ability with correct hooks, metadata, schemas, and permissions.

use_cases.title: Expose abilities to clients
use_cases.description: Configure REST visibility and verify that registered abilities appear through the expected namespace.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a missing ability
use_cases.description: Trace registration timing, metadata, route selection, JavaScript dependencies, and caching.

prompt_templates.title: Check project compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress project and determine whether the Abilities API is available. Report version constraints and required project context.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an ability
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a namespaced read-only ability for this plugin. Specify its category, registration hooks, metadata, input, output, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot REST visibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why this registered ability is missing from REST responses. Check hook order, metadata, identifiers, routes, permissions, and caches.

prompt_templates.title: Review an end-to-end integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this PHP and JavaScript Abilities API integration. Assess registration, schemas, permissions, REST exposure, client usage, tests, and compatibility.

output_examples.input: Plan a read-only site information ability for my plugin.
output: Register the category before the ability using the dedicated category hook.
Use a stable namespaced identifier and mark the ability as read-only.
Expose it through REST only when clients require access.
Define output validation and test registration plus REST visibility.

output_examples.input: Why does my ability not appear in the REST response?
output_examples.output: Check that registration runs on the ability initialization hook, the category already exists, REST visibility is enabled, and the expected route is queried.

output_examples.input: Review a data-changing ability before release.
output_examples.output: The review identifies permission checks, input validation, stable identifiers, registration timing, REST exposure, output expectations, and focused PHP and JavaScript tests.

best_practices: Register categories before abilities using the dedicated initialization hooks.
Use stable namespaced identifiers and explicit input and output schemas.
Require permission callbacks for abilities that modify data.
anti_patterns: Do not register abilities outside the documented initialization hook.
Do not expose an ability through REST without reviewing permissions and data sensitivity.
Do not change published ability identifiers without treating the change as breaking.

faq.question: Which WordPress versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets WordPress 6.9 and later, or projects using a compatible Abilities API package.

faq.question: Can it register categories and abilities?
faq.answer: It guides both tasks and explains the required category-first hook order.

faq.question: Can it help with REST visibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks REST metadata, route selection, registration timing, identifiers, and expected responses.

faq.question: Does it cover JavaScript clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends the WordPress abilities package and checks dependency bundling and client access.

faq.question: Does every ability need a permission callback?
faq.answer: Data-changing abilities should always include one. Read-only abilities still require a permission review based on exposed information.

faq.question: Does this skill run a WordPress environment?
faq.answer: No. Verification requires an available project environment, REST routes, and the project testing tools.
